idea: PQMagic's ML-DSA-87 needs about 125 KB of stack and the heap of the RAM image is split into regions of at most 112 KB, so the job could not be created. A static buffer can be registered as one more heap region.
change: suites/pqmagic_common/kemsig.c: KEMSIG_EXTRA_HEAP (heap_caps_add_region on a static array); suites/pqmagic_mldsa87 sets it to 143360.
note: Not a speed change: before, the task could not be allocated (rc -100), so there is no before value. After: FIPS 204 known-answer test passes on the device for the SHAKE variant, 12 of 12 fingerprints equal.

idea: SPHINCS-alpha's encoding table is a static array of 256-bit integers, 278 KB for the smallest set, and cannot exist in a RAM image. Rows need far fewer bytes than 32 per entry and are symmetric.
change: suites/pqmagic_sphincsa/pqc_suite/sphincsa_dp.c (per-row byte width, half rows, one heap block per row, built with a sliding sum); #ifdef PQC_COMPACT_DP block in third_party/pqmagic/sig/sphincs-a/std/wots.c.
checked: host fingerprint against the unchanged upstream table; device fingerprint for 128f
note: 128s: 583648 to 102249 bytes, 192f: 497408 to 128035 bytes. Host: identical keys and signatures to the upstream code with its static table for 128f/128s (SM3, SHA-2, SHAKE) and 192f. Device: 128f verified in all three hash families (18 of 18 fingerprints, 66 KB of heap for table and build rows); 128s not run; 192f failed, the table allocation ran out of heap (162 KB free against 128 KB table + 15 KB build rows + 20 KB job stack) and the run stopped at an assert. 192s, 256f and 256s need 332 KB or more even in compact form and were not attempted.

idea: Until the shared primitives were linked whole, the opt variant of the PQMagic suites ran the reference SM3 and Keccak. With the fast SM3 and the assembly Keccak really in the image, the SM3 and SHAKE instantiations should gain in proportion to their hashing.
change: components/prims linked with WHOLE_ARCHIVE; all PQMagic, SCloud+ and LAC suites rerun
note: ML-KEM-768 with SM3 keygen 10310 -> 7424 us. The 14 KB the backends add made three images run out of RAM: NEV-AKE (job stack 72 -> 60 KB), PQMagic's ML-DSA-87 (reserved region 143 -> 133 KB, Keccak and SHA-256 backends left out) and SCloud+-256 (SM3 family moved to its own image).

idea: The 192f image failed only because the compact table (128 KB), its two build rows (15 KB) and a 20 KB job stack did not fit the free heap together. The scheme itself needs a few KB of stack, and the image carries an SM3 backend it never calls.
change: suites/pqmagic_sphincsa/pqc_suite/sphincsa_unity.inc (PQM_STACK, default 20 KB); sphincsa_sha2_192f.c and sphincsa_shake_192f.c (10 KB); suites/pqmagic_sphincsa_192f/pqc_suite/prims_off.txt (sm3)
checked: tamper rejection + fingerprint: 12 of 12 equal the host, ref and opt agree
note: before/after are the reference and the optimized variant; before this change the suite did not run at all. Free heap at start 171844 bytes, peak heap 146108 bytes while the table is built, 7328 bytes of stack used. SHA-2 192f: keygen 375 -> 129 ms, verify 211 -> 112 ms. SHAKE 192f: keygen 1348 -> 865 ms, sign 26.0 -> 16.7 s, verify 682 -> 442 ms. The same rerun day also ran the 128s sets on the device for the first time (36 of 36 fingerprints of pqmagic_sphincsa equal the host; 106 KB of heap for the table).
